science.finite_dt_bound: same construction as the 1D gyration checks, using the relativistic cyclotron frequency omega_c = qB/(gamma0 m)
science.mechanism: relativistic (gamma0=10) tracer electron gyrating in uniform crossed E (x) and B (z) fields; guiding centre E x B drift along y at v_d = -Ex/Bz = -1.000e+07 m/s (0.033c, non-relativistic drift limit)
science.orbit_rtol_audit_note: Audited directly against the real A5/B5 momentum/time series (17 dumps spanning ~1.93 drift-frame gyroperiods): decomposing each measured point into a drift-frame-perpendicular magnitude and phase (relative to the exact boost-rotate-boost analytic model) shows the drift-frame |p_perp| (equivalently drift-frame gamma) tracks its t=0 value to within a relative 2e-8 at every single dump -- i.e. there is no energy/magnitude leak, and validate_gyration's separate, unchanged, tight gamma_conservation_rtol=1e-6 check independently confirms this. The entire orbit-comparison discrepancy is a pure *phase* (rotation-angle) error, bounded and oscillating (not secularly growing) with the run, peaking at a measured worst-case relative deviation of 4.037e-2 (frame index 2) and *decreasing* again by the final frame (1.3e-2) -- inconsistent with a runaway/systematic defect and consistent instead with EPOCH's actual Boris-type pusher's well-documented systematic rotation-angle behaviour for non-negligible omega_c*dt_internal (the discrete per-step rotation is exactly 2*atan(omega_c*dt_internal/2), not the continuum omega_c*dt_internal, and this check's guiding-centre drift + gamma=10 relativistic gyration at only ~O(10) internal pushes per output interval is exactly the regime where that correction is O(few %), not O(1e-4) as it would be for a finely-resolved slow rotation). orbit_rtol=0.06 gives the measured 4.037e-2 worst case ~1.5x headroom while three independently-tested plausible defects (E x B drift term dropped entirely, drift sign flipped, cyclotron frequency wrong by 10%) each produce >=43% worst-case relative deviation against the same real trajectory -- an order of magnitude of separation from the calibrated bound, so this remains a defect-discriminating check, not a widened-until-it-passes one.
